teaser.text: Berkshire Hathaway owns businesses that sell insurance, transport, energy, manufactured goods, distribution and services. It also owns shares in other companies, but those investments work differently from the businesses it controls.

blocks.heading: Where could Berkshire Hathaway’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The bear, base and bull cases carry probabilities of 25%, 55% and 20%; the bear and bull values are $419.23 and $774.86. Third-quarter 2026 results, expected November 2, will test insurance, railroad, utility and manufacturing performance. On November 3, 2026, the Oregon Supreme Court will hear oral argument in PacifiCorp’s class-action case, in which people with similar claims sue together.

The weighted price reaches $527.08 in October 2027, including dividends, for a 3% return from today’s $511.05. It reaches $560.37 in October 2028, a 10% return, and $595.71 in October 2029, a 17% return. Dividends do not contribute because every case assumes no payout.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Berkshire Hathaway, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires several pressures to arrive together: catastrophe losses, adverse reserve development, wildfire liabilities, slow utility recovery and fewer attractive investments. The multiple contracts as investors question growth and recent insurance profitability. The price falls from $431.15 in October 2027 to $419.23 in October 2029. Its 25% probability reflects meaningful exposure to these risks, while Berkshire’s diversification makes a deeper collapse less likely.

The bull case requires sustained underwriting discipline, better BNSF execution, timely BHE recovery and favorable investment marks. Management then uses surplus cash for undervalued repurchases or investments, raising per-share value. The price rises from $598.08 to $774.86. The probability is 20% because several businesses must execute well at once.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Berkshire Hathaway really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash provides a necessary second test. Berkshire generated about US$46.0 billion of operating cash flow in 2025. It spent US$20.9 billion on capital assets, leaving roughly US$25.1 billion before other investing and financing needs. That remainder is not automatically distributable: railroads and utilities must replace assets, while insurance cash also reflects policyholder funding and claims.

blocks.heading: What has Berkshire Hathaway guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: The commitments now visible describe financial resilience more clearly than future profit. Berkshire will not repurchase shares if consolidated cash, equivalents and Treasury bills fall below US$30,000 million. BHE and BNSF expect to spend US$8,600 million in the remainder of 2026.

blocks.heading: What do Berkshire Hathaway’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter improved, but currency accounting amplified the headline. Revenue and operating earnings rose, while net income and diluted EPS benefited from investment movements and comparison with a quarter containing an impairment.

The improvement was uneven. BNSF, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and manufacturing, service and retailing improved, while insurance underwriting and insurance investment income declined. GEICO’s underwriting earnings fell, showing why a stronger group total does not mean every subsidiary improved. OxyChem’s acquisition also contributed to manufacturing growth, so not all of that progress came from existing operations.

blocks.heading: What should people watch in Berkshire Hathaway’s next results?

paragraphs.text: PacifiCorp, Berkshire’s utility, agreed to a US$575 million federal wildfire settlement, but its separate Oregon class-action case continued. The Oregon Supreme Court scheduled oral argument for November 3, 2026. An accrued loss is an accounting estimate, not a final court award: appeals can delay payment, and the eventual amount can differ. Litigation can therefore compete with safety upgrades and affect borrowing costs.

The decisive evidence will connect spending with outcomes: construction progress with usable capacity, new capacity with customer demand, and operating profit with cash generation. If those links hold, Abel will have shown that continuity is more than a promise; it is a method for financing Berkshire’s next chapter.
